title: Census: per-packet detection coverage before forecasting recall
description:
Measure how many components and data flows the engine detects per corpus packet, before anyone forecasts what the identity ruling buys.

**Why.** The measured case for structured component identity (see KDATAP-00e64a) shows the vocabulary fix working: on `easy-school`, identity-only matching goes from 1/3 to 2/3 when assets and actors are keyed on subtype. But `flask-login` @ `c8bba84` emits **zero components** — 11 files ingested, nothing detected — while its gold claims two positives. No identity scheme rescues that.

The 481-of-563 figure is the share of component gold whose *vocabulary* becomes satisfiable. It is not a recall forecast, because it assumes the component was detected at all. Nobody knows the detection rate.

**Method.** For each of the 29 packets, at its manifest commit and scope: files ingested, components emitted, data flows emitted, and the count of gold positives whose subject the engine emitted under each of the three identity schemes. No scoring, no eligibility, no spans — a coverage census, not a baseline.

**What it decides.** If detection is broadly healthy and the misses are vocabulary, the harness epic is the right investment and the ruling pays for itself. If the engine emits nothing on a large share of packets, then component recall is a detector problem wearing a vocabulary costume, and the sequencing in this programme should be revisited before 750 adjudications are spent.

Depends on the materialize fix, or on cloning packets by hand as the two spot checks did.
